summary.text: PETG-ESD is an anti-static PETG copolyester. Makers sell it for electronics and semiconductor uses where electrostatic discharge matters. It is amorphous as printed, so it softens at its glass transition: its HDT at 0.45 MPa is 75 °C. On the H2C it prints at 250⁠–⁠260 °C, and a maker warns that nozzle temperature and print orientation strongly affect surface resistivity.

items.text: The ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) safety of PETG-ESD filament can degrade over time, depending on environmental factors like humidity, temperature, and exposure to dust or contaminants. PETG-ESD filaments contain conductive additives, which can wear off or lose effectiveness due to surface abrasion or environmental wear. Typically, the ESD-safe properties should remain intact for 1-2 years under controlled conditions, but regular testing is recommended to ensure continued ESD performance. Storing parts in a clean, dry environment can help maintain their ESD properties longer.
